messages.subject: Poppr has updated to version 1.0.6
messages.body_plain:
This is a simple patch to fix a bug that occurred with the new version of ape. It is only necessary to update to this version if you plan to update ape.

The source is up on CRAN now and the windows and mac binaries should be there shortly.

Cheers,
Zhian

messages.subject: Minimum Spanning Networks (MSNs)
messages.body_plain:
Hi all

I have a doubt about interpretation of my MSN.

I am studying the genetic structure of a fungal pathogen with Multilocus ISSR markers. I got a distance matrix and a MSN form my data set. However, I saw in the manual that the Bruvo's distance is exclusive for microsatellite markers. So, I understand that in my MSN, edge thickness and color are not proportional to Bruvo's distance, as in the case of microsatellite data. Then, what do the edge thickness and color mean in my MSN?

Thanks in advance for your help
David

messages.subject: Re: Minimum Spanning Networks (MSNs)
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

The edge widths and shades MSNs from poppr are always proportional to the distance input. Smaller distances will give thick, dark edges and shorter distances will give light, thin edges. This is assuming that you chose another distance and used the function poppr.msn() to produce your MSN.

Hope that answers your question,
Zhian

Thanks again

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Re: Minimum Spanning Networks (MSNs)
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

I see now where the confusion lies. After looking back at the manual, it appears that I was caught copying and pasting. Figure 19's legend should read:

> Figure 19: Minimum Spanning Network representing 4 simulated populations. Each node represents a different multi locus genotype (MLG). Node sizes and colors correspond to the number of individuals and population membership, respectively. Edge thickness and color are proportional to genetic distance. Edge lengths are arbitrary.

Thank you for alerting me to this. It will change in the next version of poppr.

So, to answer your question: No, they are not proportinal to Bruvo's distance, but they are proportional to the genetic distance (in this case, absolute genetic distance).

Cheers,
Zhian
